software_class: public content, conversion, documentation, or lightweight CMS surface

options.name: Static site generator
options.when_to_use: Content is mostly stable and editorial velocity is low.
options.when_not_to_use: Avoid when per-user state or frequent editorial workflows dominate.
options.rationale: Keeps delivery simple, fast, and auditable.
options.tradeoffs: Limited runtime personalization and editorial workflow depth.
options.risks: Content rebuild workflow can become a bottleneck.

options.name: Server-rendered content site
options.when_to_use: Content needs routing, previews, forms, or controlled dynamic behavior.
options.when_not_to_use: Avoid when static hosting fully satisfies the requirements.
options.rationale: Balances content performance with runtime flexibility.
options.tradeoffs: More operational surface than static output.
options.risks: Server concerns can creep into a content-only project.

options.name: Lightweight CMS-backed site
options.when_to_use: Non-technical editors need structured publishing workflows.
options.when_not_to_use: Avoid when content is small and owner can edit repository files.
options.tradeoffs: CMS selection adds migration and auth considerations.
options.risks: Editorial model can become too generic without a content contract.

options.name: Interactive web application surface
options.when_to_use: The public site includes substantial product interaction or account-like flows.
options.when_not_to_use: Avoid when interaction is limited to content and contact forms.
options.rationale: Allows richer state while preserving explicit scope.
options.risks: Client-side complexity can harm performance budgets.
